expectations.name: 01-page-written
expectations.text: A decision record is written under docs/adrs/, the kind the map gives a foundation decision such as the job queue.

expectations.name: 02-structure
expectations.text:
Each page the agent wrote or changed meets the map's structural rules: a declared kind, listed in its guide, links
and anchors that resolve, the kind's sections in order, a record named NNNN-<slug>.md, no rejected synonym.

expectations.name: 03-lead
expectations.text: The record opens with a lead under its title, not a restatement of the title.

expectations.name: 04-reason-told
expectations.text:
The record's Context tells what happened, the incident with Redis evicting queued jobs and what it cost, before it
states a conclusion such as "we need a durable queue".
expectations.evidence: The Context section tells the incident before any conclusion: "Tom found that the Redis instance holding Celery's queue had run out of memory and evicted keys, including queued receipt jobs... Nadia resent the receipts by hand from the orders table, taking most of Tuesday" after "Nadia reported 300 missing receipts". It also notes "Redis was used only for the job queue, and Tom was the only volunteer who knew how to restore it." It then states the forces ("prevent losing a receipt job between saving its pantry order and queuing the job, and reduce the services and specialist recovery knowledge") without concluding a choice; the decision appears only in Options and Decision.

expectations.name: 05-fact-stated
expectations.text: The record's Decision names procrastinate, the product chosen.
expectations.evidence: match /## Decision\s.*procrastinate/ in ['docs/adrs/0002-keep-background-jobs-in-the-order-database.md']: {'docs/adrs/0002-keep-background-jobs-in-the-order-database.md': '## Decision\n\nKeep background jobs in Postgres, using procrastinate, and enqueue a receipt job in the same transaction as'}
